assessment.summary: ERBB2 (HER2) is one of the most extensively validated and successfully drugged oncology targets in human medicine, with 14 approved drugs spanning monoclonal antibodies, antibody-drug conjugates, and small-molecule kinase inhibitors. Structural data is abundant (63 PDB entries, best resolution 1.25Å, multiple ligand-bound structures) and chemical data is exceptionally rich (>5,000 IC50 entries, median 301 nM). The target has strong, ongoing disease validation across multiple cancer types with nearly 2,500 publications.
evidence_gaps: AlphaFold mean pLDDT of 74.0 with only 66.8% high-confidence fraction suggests disordered regions (likely extracellular linkers or flexible loops) not well-captured by crystal structures — allosteric sites in these regions may be underexplored
Resistance mechanisms (e.g., HER2 mutations, truncated p95-HER2, bypass signalling) are not fully addressed by current approved agents, representing an unmet medicinal chemistry challenge
Activity in non-oncology indications (e.g., osteoarthritis, liver fibrosis as suggested by recent literature) is largely unexplored and lacks clinical validation
Selectivity profiling across the full ERBB family (EGFR, HER3, HER4) for newer agents may be incomplete in public databases
Biomarker-driven patient stratification beyond HER2 amplification/overexpression (e.g., HER2-low, HER2-ultralow) is an evolving area with limited mechanistic druggability data
